Roman emperor from 193 to 211, the first from Africa. He was born at Leptis Magna in today's Libya, to a family of Punic and Italian roots, and rose through the usual offices under Marcus Aurelius.

In the Year of the Five Emperors, 193, he marched on Rome and then beat his rivals Pescennius Niger in the east and Clodius Albinus in Gaul. He founded the Severan dynasty.

  • He fought the Parthians, sacked their capital Ctesiphon and added a new province in Mesopotamia.
  • He raised army pay and made the army bigger, which made the state lean even harder on the soldiers.
  • He married Julia Domna, a Syrian from Emesa.

He spent his last years in Britain fighting the Caledonians beyond Hadrian's Wall and died at York in 211. His sons Caracalla and Geta were to share power; within a year Caracalla had Geta killed.
sum: Roman emperor from 193 to 211, the first from Africa. He was born at Leptis Magna in today's Libya, to a family of Punic and Italian roots, and rose through the usual offices under Marcus Aurelius.
